Consider a journey by a car represented by the graph given below in three parts A, B and C. The speed of the car in these parts is \(v_a\), \(v_b\) and \(v_c\), respectively :

[Graph: distance (m) on the vertical axis against time (s) on the horizontal axis. Part A rises from the origin with a small, gentle slope; part B then rises much more steeply; part C thereafter rises with a very small slope, almost flat.]

Which one of the following is correct in this case ?

In the following simplified diagram of a plant cell, five parts/organelles are marked from 1 to 5 :

[Diagram: a plant cell drawn as a polygon whose boundary is a pair of parallel lines, an outer line and an inner line. Two leader arrows, 1 and 2, point outwards from this pair of boundary lines at the top right, arrow 1 to the left of arrow 2; at print resolution the two tails cannot be told apart reliably, so which of them rests on the outer line and which on the inner is not determinable from the figure. Arrow 3 points out to the top left, its tail resting on a stack of coiled, ribbon-like membranes lying in the upper part of the cell. Arrow 4 points out to the left, its tail resting on a small round shaded body that contains a dark dot. Arrow 5 points out to the bottom left, its tail resting on the large grey lobed body that occupies the centre and lower part of the cell.]

Which one of the following correctly represents the above parts/organelles ?

The following diagram shows a pendulum at different positions. Which one of the following statement is true ?

[Diagram: a pendulum hangs from a single point on a horizontal support. Five strings run from that pivot down to five bob positions drawn inside a rectangular frame, marked P, Q, R, S and T from left to right. R is the central bob, hanging vertically below the pivot, and is the lowest of the five. Q and S lie on either side of R and hang a little higher than R. P and T are the outermost bobs, on the extreme left and extreme right, and hang the highest of the five.]
